source_text: Ἣν εἶδον, ἀδελφοί, τοιαύτη. νηστεύσας πολλάκις καὶ δεηθεὶς τοῦ κυρίου, ἵνα μοι φανερώσῃ τὴν ἀποκάλυψιν, ἥν μοι ἐπηγγείλατο δεῖξαι διὰ τῆς πρεσβυτέρας ἐκείνης, αὐτῇ τῇ νυκτί μοι ὦπται ἡ πρεσβυτέρα καὶ εἶπέν μοι: Ἐπεὶ οὕτως ἐνδεὴς εἶ καὶ σπουδαῖος εἰς τὸ γνῶναι πάντα, ἐλθὲ εἰς τὸν ἀγρόν, ὅπου χονδρίζεις, καὶ περὶ ὥραν πέμπτην ἐμφανισθήσομαί σοι καὶ δείξω σοι, ἃ δεῖ σε ἰδεῖν. ἠρώτησα αὐτὴν λέγων: Κυρία, εἰς ποῖον τόπον τοῦ ἀγροῦ; Ὅπου, φησίν, θέλεις. ἐξελεξάμην τόπον καλὸν ἀνακεχωρηκότα. πρὶν δὲ λαλῆσαι αὐτῇ καὶ εἰπεῖν τὸν τόπον, λέγει μοι: Ἥξω ἐκεῖ, ὅπου θέλεις. ἐγενόμην οὖν, ἀδελφοί, εἰς τὸν ἀγρὸν καὶ συνεψήφισα τὰς ὥρας καὶ ἦλθον εἰς τὸν τόπον, ὅπου διεταξάμην αὐτῇ ἐλθεῖν, καὶ βλέπω συμψέλιον κείμενον ἐλεφάντινον, καὶ ἐπὶ τοῦ συμψελίου ἔκειτο κερβικάριον λινοῦν καὶ ἐπάνω λέντιον ἐξηπλωμένον λινοῦν καρπάσιον. ἰδὼν ταῦτα κείμενα καὶ μηδένα ὄντα ἐν τῷ τόπῳ ἔκθαμβος ἐγενόμην, καὶ ὡσεὶ τρόμος με ἔλαβεν καὶ αἱ τρίχες μου ὀρθαί: καὶ ὡσεὶ φρίκη μοι προσῆλθεν μόνου μου ὄντος. ἐν ἐμαυτῷ οὖν γενόμενος καὶ μνησθεὶς τῆς δόξης τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ λαβὼν θάρσος, θεὶς τὰ γόνατα ἐξωμολογούμην τῷ κυρίῳ πάλιν τὰς ἁμαρτίας μου ὡς καὶ πρότερον. ἡ δὲ ἦλθεν μετὰ νεανίσκων ἕξ, οὓς καὶ πρότερον ἑωράκειν, καὶ ἐστάθη μοι καὶ κατηκροᾶτο προσευχομένου καὶ ἐξομολογουμένου τῷ κυρίῳ τὰς ἁμαρτίας μου. καὶ ἁψαμένη μου λέγει: Ἑρμᾶ, παῦσαι περὶ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν σου πάντα ἐρωτῶν: ἐρώτα καὶ περὶ δικαιοσύνης, ἵνα λάβῃς μέρος τι ἐξ αὐτῆς εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου. καὶ ἐξεγείρει με τῆς χειρὸς καὶ ἄγει με πρὸς τὸ συμψέλιον καὶ λέγει τοῖς νεανίσκοις: Ὑπάγετε καὶ οἰκοδομεῖτε. καὶ μετὰ τὸ ἀναχωρῆσαι τοὺς νεανίσκους καὶ μόνων ἡμῶν γεγονότων λέγει μοι: Κάθισον ὧδε. λέγω αὐτῇ: Κυρία, ἄφες τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους πρῶτον καθίσαι. Ὅ σοι λέγω, φησίν, κάθισον. θέλοντος οὖν μου καθίσαι εἰς τὰ δεξιὰ μέρη οὐκ εἴασέ με, ἀλλ’ ἐννεύει μοι τῇ χειρί, ἵνα εἰς τὰ ἀριστερὰ μέρη καθίσω. διαλογιζομένου μου οὖν καὶ λυπουμένου, ὅτι οὐκ εἴασέ με εἰς τὰ δεξιὰ μέρη καθίσαι, λέγει μοι: Λυπῇ, Ἑρμᾶ; ὁ εἰς τὰ δεξιὰ μέρη τόπος ἄλλων ἐστίν, τῶν ἤδη εὐαρεστηκότων τῷ θεῷ καὶ παθόντων εἵνεκα τοῦ ὀνόματος: σοὶ δὲ πολλὰ λείπει ἵνα μετ’ αὐτῶν καθίσῃς: ἀλλὰ ὡς μένεις τῇ ἁπλότητί σου, μεῖνον, καὶ καθιῇ μετ’ αὐτῶν καὶ ὅσοι ἐὰν ἐργάσωνται τὰ ἐκείνων ἔργα καὶ ὑπενέγκωσιν, ἃ καὶ ἐκεῖνοι ὑπήνεγκαν. Τί, φημί, ὑπήνεγκαν; Ἄκουε, φησίν: μάστιγας, φυλακάς, θλίψεις μεγάλας, σταυρούς, θηρία εἵνεκεν τοῦ ὀνόματος: διὰ τοῦτο ἐκείνων ἐστὶν τὰ δεξιὰ μέρη τοῦ ἁγιάσματος καὶ ὃς ἐὰν πάθῃ διὰ τὸ ὄνομα: τῶν δὲ λοιπῶν τὰ ἀριστερὰ μέρη ἐστίν.
pass_a_gloss: What I saw, brothers, was the following. Having fasted many times and prayed to the Lord that He might reveal to me the revelation which He had promised to show me through that elderly woman, on that very night the elderly woman appeared to me and said to me: Since you are so needy and eager to know all things, come to the field where you work and around the fifth hour I will appear to you and show you what you must see. I asked her saying: Lady, to what place in the field? Wherever you wish, she says. I chose a beautiful secluded place. But before I spoke to her and told her the place, she says to me: I will be there wherever you wish. So I went, brothers, to the field and counted the hours and came to the place where I had told her to come, and I saw a linen cushion lying there and on the cushion a linen kerchief was lying and above it a linen cloth was spread out, a carpet. Seeing these things lying there and no one being in the place, I was amazed and a sort of trembling seized me and my hairs stood on end: and a sort of horror approached me, I being alone. So I came to myself and remembered the glory of God and took courage, and putting my knees on the ground, I confessed to the Lord again my sins, as also before. And she came with six young men, whom I had also seen before, and stood by me and looked at me as I was praying and confessing my sins to the Lord. And touching me, she says: Hermas, stop inquiring about all your sins: inquire also about righteousness, so that you may receive a part of it for your household. And she rouses me with her hand and leads me to the cushion and says to the young men: Go and build. And after the young men departed and we were alone, she says to me: Sit here. I say to her: Lady, allow the elders to sit first. Whatever I tell you, she says, sit. So when I wanted to sit on the right side, she did not allow me, but signals to me with her hand to sit on the left side. As I was reasoning and being grieved that she did not allow me to sit on the right side, she says to me: Are you grieved, Hermas? The place on the right side belongs to others, who have already pleased God and suffered for the sake of the name: you still lack much in order to sit with them: but as you remain in your simplicity, remain, and you will sit with them and all who will do their works and bear what they also bore. What, I say, did they bear? Listen, she says: floggings, imprisonments, great tribulations, crosses, wild beasts for the sake of the name: for this reason the right side of the sanctuary belongs to them, and to whoever suffers for the name: but the left side belongs to the rest.
pass_b_english: Brothers, this is what I saw. I had fasted many times and prayed to the Lord, asking Him to reveal the revelation He had promised to show me through that elderly woman. On that very night she appeared to me and said, "Since you are so needy and eager to know everything, come to the field where you work; around the fifth hour I will appear to you and show you what you must see." I asked her, "Lady, what place in the field?" She answered, "Wherever you wish." So I chose a beautiful, secluded spot. But before I could speak and tell her the place, she said, "I will be there, wherever you wish." I went to the field, brothers, counted the hours, and arrived at the spot I had designated for her to meet me. There I saw an ivory couch lying on the ground. On the couch lay a linen kerchief, and over it a linen carpet was spread out. Seeing these things there with no one present, I was overwhelmed with amazement. Trembling seized me, my hair stood on end, and a cold horror came over me because I was alone. I pulled myself together, remembered the glory of God, and took courage. I fell to my knees and confessed my sins to the Lord once again, just as I had done before. Then she arrived with six young men, the same ones I had seen before. They stood beside me and watched me while I was praying and confessing my sins to the Lord. She touched me and said, "Hermas, stop asking about all your sins. Ask also about righteousness, so that you may receive a share of it for your household." She took me by the hand, raised me up, and led me to the couch. Then she said to the young men, "Go and build." After they left and we were alone, she told me, "Sit here." I replied, "Lady, let the elders sit first." She said, "Do whatever I tell you; sit." When I tried to sit on the right side, she would not allow it. Instead, she signaled with her hand for me to sit on the left. As I puzzled over this and felt grieved that she would not let me sit on the right, she asked, "Are you grieved, Hermas? The place on the right belongs to others — those who have already pleased God and suffered for the sake of the Name. You still lack much to sit with them. But if you remain in your simplicity, you will remain and will sit with them, along with everyone who does their works and endures what they also endured." I asked, "What did they endure?" She said, "Listen: floggings, imprisonments, great tribulations, crosses, wild beasts — all for the sake of the Name. For this reason the right side of the sanctuary belongs to them, and to whoever suffers for the Name. The left side belongs to the rest."

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text. Pass A preserves the nuances of the Greek (e.g., 'linen cushion' for συμψέλιον, 'linen kerchief' for κερβικάριον, and 'linen cloth' for λέντιον), and Pass B provides a fluent rendering that remains faithful to the source. The distinction between the right and left sides and the reasons for them (suffering for the Name) is correctly preserved. All clauses, including the list of sufferings, are accounted for.

The translation accurately reflects the Greek text, preserving the meaning, structure, and key terms. All citations and references are correctly matched. No errors in source identity, completeness, negation, agency, modality, doctrine, or scripture are found.
